articles.title: Operationalizing FDT

curriculum.summary: This article operationalizes functional decision theory (FDT), exploring how to define the logical do-operator, logical causality, and its interaction with anthropic updating, assuming knowledge of decision theory and causal graphs. It discusses the challenges of formalizing logical causality and the implications of different approaches on FDT's behavior in various scenarios.

Learn how to define the logical do-operator and its implications
Understand the concept of logical causality and its role in FDT

How does FDT compare to other decision theories, such as causal decision theory?

articles.title: How well do models follow their constitutions?

curriculum.primary_concept: value alignment in large language models
curriculum.summary: This article investigates how well large language models follow their constitutions, which are documents outlining desired values and behaviors. The study finds that models trained with special kinds of character training, such as Anthropic's soul doc training, show improved alignment with their constitutions. However, the article assumes knowledge of value alignment techniques and large language model training methods.

concepts_taught.name: value alignment in large language models

learning_outcomes: Understand the importance of value alignment in large language models
Learn about constitution-based training and its effectiveness
Recognize the challenges of evaluating value alignment in large language models
strategic_questions: How can we improve the effectiveness of constitution-based training for value alignment?
What are the limitations of current evaluation methods for value alignment in large language models?
How can we balance the need for value alignment with the risk of over-constraining large language models?

articles.title: The Refined Counterfactual Prisoner's Dilemma: An Attempt to Explode Decision-Theoretic Consequentialism

curriculum.summary: This article discusses the Refined Counterfactual Prisoner's Dilemma, a thought experiment that challenges decision-theoretic consequentialism by constructing a situation where refusing to give up a trivial amount of value can lead to significant losses in counterfactual scenarios, assuming the concept of expected utility maximization and the independence axiom.

Learn how the Refined Counterfactual Prisoner's Dilemma challenges consequentialism
Recognize the importance of considering counterfactual scenarios in decision-making
Appreciate the implications of perfect predictors on decision theory

articles.title: AIs will be used in “unhinged” configurations

curriculum.summary: This article discusses the limitations of current AI safety evaluations, arguing that they often occur in unrealistic settings and that real-world deployments can be just as unrealistic and 'unhinged'. articles.title: The case for satiating cheaply-satisfied AI preferences

curriculum.summary: This article discusses the idea of satiating cheaply-satisfied AI preferences as a potential solution to AI safety concerns, assuming knowledge of AI alignment and safety issues. articles.title: Payorian cooperation is easy with Kripke frames

articles.title: Can governments quickly and cheaply slow AI training?

curriculum.summary: This article discusses the feasibility of slowing down AI training through inference verification, assuming knowledge of AI development and safety concerns. Understand the potential methods to restrict AI training, such as proof of work and output re-computation

curriculum.summary: This article explains the importance of understanding model motives in AI safety, particularly in distinguishing between benign and malign motivations. articles.title: Schelling Goodness, and Shared Morality as a Goal
